tagline: Mic-check your taste: comparisons-first personal ratings for books (Phase 1), expandable to films + restaurants (Phase 4+).

core_metaphors: Mic check: quick calibration to find your true signal
Double check: confirm preference by head-to-head comparisons

north_star.goal: Validate that reviewing against yourself via A/B comparisons feels delightful and produces scores you trust.
success_metrics: User completes a 10-comparison sprint in < 60 seconds.
After ~30 comparisons, user's top 5 and bottom 5 feel 'basically right' without manual star entry.
User returns within 48 hours to add an item or do 5 more comparisons.

development_principles: Library is source of truth: only explicitly added items participate in scoring and recommendations.
Comparisons are the primitive action; stars are derived presentation.
Deterministic scoring: no AI decides ratings. (AI, if ever used, can only label metadata once at ingestion.)
Version everything that affects meaning (rating curve, taxonomy); never silently rewrite history.
Web-first, mobile-responsive: on small screens, only one primary surface at a time.
invariants: Persist raw comparisons as the durable truth; recompute scores from comparisons deterministically.
Display uses quarter-star rounding (0.25) with hysteresis to prevent jitter.
Expose a stacked ranking signal: rank_score_raw (0.00–5.00, 2 decimals) + rank/percentile.
Avoid false precision in list views (quarter stars); reserve decimals for detail views.

phase_1.name: checkcheck MVP (Books Only)
phase_1.goal: Prove the comparisons-first loop is fun, fast, and trustworthy. Ship scoring + hysteresis + stacked ranking.
non_goals: No public profiles, feeds, follows, or sharing.
No films/restaurants yet (unless needed for UI scaffolding only).

epics.name: Library + Item Ingestion
epics.outcome: User can build a personal library quickly and confidently.
scope: Manual add (title, author) as baseline.
Import from Goodreads/StoryGraph (CSV) via unified Import entry; store legacy ratings/reviews for provenance but never use or show them in ranking UI.
Optional: external search integration (later) behind a flag.
Statuses: want / reading / finished; finished_at.
Library sub-views: Want to read (saved queue), Unplaced (finished but not yet rated), and Finished (rated history).
Want enrichment (Phase 1): suggested type + user tags (context only; never affects scoring).
Metadata ingestion (Phase 1): preserve Open Library raw subjects on items for future taxonomy expansion.
De-dupe strategy documented (work vs edition).
acceptance_criteria: User can add 10 items in < 3 minutes.
Library list renders quickly and remains usable on mobile.

epics.name: Compare Session
epics.outcome: User can complete a 10-comparison sprint with near-zero friction.
scope: Compare surface (A vs B) with primary actions: A wins / B wins / Skip / Undo.
Compare input: whole card is tappable; buttons are secondary affordance.
Pending-lock: prevent interleavings while saving/recomputing (A/B/Skip/Undo).
Motion: calm press + crossfade only; respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Gate compare until 5 active finished items exist (initiation milestone).
Persist comparison rows (user_id, a, b, winner|null, created_at).
Pair selection: meaningful matchups (see docs/PAIR_SELECTION.md).
acceptance_criteria: 10 comparisons can be completed in < 60 seconds.
Rapid double-tap cannot create two comparisons.
Undo reverses the most recent comparison reliably.
Skip does not corrupt scoring.

epics.name: Deterministic Scoring + Display
epics.outcome: Scores feel true, stable, and culturally intuitive.
scope: Compute per-item strength (Elo) deterministically from comparisons.
Convert strength→percentile→rank_score_raw via versioned curve.
Compute quarter-star candidate and apply hysteresis to stars_display.
Stars display should be visually unambiguous (SVG quarter-fill).
Stacked rating UI: quarter stars + rank_score_raw + rank/percentile + confidence (comparison count).
acceptance_criteria: Stars do not jitter near boundaries (hysteresis tests pass).
Sorting by rank_score_raw is stable and consistent.
Detail view explains 'relative to your library' clearly.

epics.name: Item Detail + Trust Tools
epics.outcome: When something feels off, the fix is obvious and doesn't feel like debugging.
scope: Item detail shows: rating stack, comparison history, key wins/losses.
Actions: 'Do 3 more comparisons' and 'Re-seed ratings' (reset derived scores without deleting comparisons, or optional reset comparisons).
Confidence indicator (based on comps count) and how-to-improve prompt.
acceptance_criteria: User can understand why an item ranks where it does.
User can correct an 'off' ranking by doing a few more comparisons.

epics.name: Tuning Harness + Instrumentation
epics.outcome: You can tune generosity + hysteresis confidently using real usage traces.
scope: Local tuning page or script that simulates comparisons and visualizes distribution.
Event logging (local-first OK) for: comparisons completed, session length, undo usage, re-seed usage.
Curve versioning and migration notes.
acceptance_criteria: You can adjust the curve anchors and see distribution changes immediately.
You can detect jitter/regressions in a repeatable way.

phase_2.name: Mobile-first UX + Bottom Tabs (Books)
phase_2.goal: Make the app feel native on mobile: bottom tabs for the core Library flows (Add book, Want, Ranking, Discover stub). After the UX is squared away, tune Elo parameters using real traces.
entry_criteria: Phase 1 loop validated (repeat usage + trust in scores).
Compare pending-lock + calm motion feel premium on mobile.
Ranking order is stable across refreshes (no jitter surprises).

epics.name: Bottom Tabs (Mobile-first Library Shell)
epics.outcome: Mobile navigation is one-handed and predictable, with four tabs: Add book, Want to read, My library ranking, Discover.
scope: Show a bottom tab bar on mobile for: Add book, Want to read, My library ranking, Discover.
Treat tabs as Library sub-views (do not introduce a new primary surface).
Compare remains a focused surface; hide the tab bar during Compare.
Detail is presented as a focused surface; Back returns to the originating tab/task state.
Discover tab is a Phase 2 stub (copy + CTA), with real functionality in Phase 3.
acceptance_criteria: On mobile, switching between Add/Wanted/Ranking is < 1s and preserves scroll state.
Compare still feels focused (no accidental tab switches mid-session).
Back behavior is consistent and never loses the in-progress Compare session state.

epics.name: Add book (Tab) — Fast Ingestion
epics.outcome: Adding a book is the fastest, most obvious action in the app.
scope: Search-first add with manual fallback.
Immediately choose status (want/reading/finished) with low-friction defaults.
After adding as finished, offer the obvious next step: Place / Mic check (depending on state).
acceptance_criteria: A new user can add 10 books in < 2 minutes on mobile.
The next action after adding is always clear (compare, place, or continue adding).

epics.name: Want to read (Tab) — Queue Control
epics.outcome: The want list feels like a lightweight reading queue, not a junk drawer.
scope: Sort and quick actions (start reading, mark finished, remove).
Lightweight organization that stays user-owned (tags are OK; no algorithmic reordering).
acceptance_criteria: Users can move items through want→reading→finished in a few taps.
Want list remains fast at 200+ items.

epics.name: My library ranking (Tab) — Browse + Place
epics.outcome: Finished rankings feel trustworthy and easy to browse; placement is always one tap away.
scope: Ranking list view is the default 'Finished' browse experience.
Show quarter-stars (list) and stacked rating context on tap (detail).
Make Unplaced items obvious and easy to place (3 comparisons).
Keep 'Mic check' available as a fast calibration sprint.
acceptance_criteria: Users can find their top 10 and bottom 10 quickly on mobile.
Unplaced items are hard to miss and easy to resolve.

epics.name: Compare feedback polish (Post-Tab UX)
epics.outcome: Compare feels tactile and calm: immediate feedback, clear pending state, no noise.
scope: Inline 'Saving…' progress state (thresholded) and honest save failure UX.
Haptics default ON with a distinct Undo pattern.
Discoverable in-Compare Feedback control (no new primary surface).
No routine success toasts in Compare.
acceptance_criteria: Tap→visual feedback is immediate; tap→next-pair p90 remains strong.
Pending-lock blocks interleavings; blocked taps do not feel broken.
Haptics can be toggled off and stays off.

epics.name: Elo tuning (After UX is squared away)
epics.outcome: Comparisons produce rankings that feel stable and intuitive across library sizes.
scope: Tune Elo parameters (K, initialization, any scaling) using real exported traces.
Define a repeatable tuning harness and acceptance thresholds (speed, stability, distribution).
Document parameter changes explicitly (no silent curve rewrites).
acceptance_criteria: Top/bottom feel 'basically right' with fewer comparisons (without increasing star jitter).
Session speed targets remain met after tuning.

phase_3.name: Discover (Books) — Preference Signals + Recommendations
phase_3.goal: Recommend books and surface preference signals using the user's own rankings, without diluting trust (no AI decides ratings; everything is explainable and evidence-backed).
entry_criteria: Phase 2 mobile shell shipped (Discover tab exists as a stub).
Sufficient finished items + comparisons to support non-noisy signals (minimum thresholds defined).
Enough metadata coverage (length/subjects/language) to avoid making up stories.

epics.name: Preference Signals (Explainable)
epics.outcome: Users can see what their library suggests they like (e.g., long books, fiction, translated) with clear evidence and confidence.
scope: Derive signals from metadata (subjects, language/translation, length, genre proxies).
Only surface a signal when thresholds are met; show confidence and examples from the library.
Always phrase as relative preferences ("you tend to prefer…"), never objective truth.
acceptance_criteria: Signals feel accurate to users and are easy to challenge/verify via comparisons.
No signal is shown without sufficient supporting examples.

epics.name: Recommendations (Discover Feed)
epics.outcome: Discover recommends books with a clear 'why this' and an easy add-to-want action.
scope: Candidate sourcing (catalog/search) and ranking using preference signals.
Explain each recommendation with 1–2 reasons tied to the user's library.
Controls: add to want, hide/not interested, and simple filters.
acceptance_criteria: Users understand why a recommendation appeared in one glance.
Discover drives meaningful add-to-want actions without degrading trust in rankings.

epics.name: Discover UX + Guardrails
epics.outcome: Discover feels helpful and safe, not manipulative.
scope: Truth-first copy and disclaimers: recommendations are suggestions; rankings remain comparisons-first.
Empty and cold-start states that teach how to get better recs (finish + compare more).
Privacy posture: signals derived from local library; no public feed by default.
acceptance_criteria: Discover has a clear next action even when empty.
Users do not interpret Discover as 'the app rated this for me'.

phase_4.name: Cross-Domain Expansion + Similarity Models
phase_4.goal: Expand beyond books (films/restaurants) and explore cross-domain taste overlaps and similarity-driven recommendations.
entry_criteria: Phase 1–3 loop validated (repeat usage + trust in scores + Discover usefulness).
Sufficient data per user to form robust user vectors (or a strong cold-start strategy).

epics.name: Shared Taste Taxonomy
scope: Define a strict, shared vibe taxonomy (energy, tone, novelty, texture, pace, social mode).
Add domain-specific metadata layers (genre/cuisine/etc).
Version taxonomy and store labels as immutable per item version.

epics.name: User Vectors + Nearest Neighbors
scope: Derive user vectors from ratings + tags across domains.
kNN similarity + explanations ('you both love cozy + witty').
Cross-domain 'bridge' experiments (book→film→restaurant).

epics.name: Tabular Predictive Models
scope: Baselines: kNN, random forest/GBDT for like/dislike.
Time-split evaluation, context leakage prevention for restaurants.
Promotion path to matrix factorization / factorization machines if needed.
